There are usually not many skilled professionals available in the communities we select to work in. Those available usually cannot afford to travel to far off places in search of work. We therefore intend to provide educational and training facilities for these skilled professionals so that they develop their skills further. This will be in form of vocational skills, construction, teaching skills, art and crafts, photography and events organizing, all in line with their interests. Community resource centers The construction of the community centers in the slums we work in will be aimed at not only providing shelter to the families but will also be aimed at sensitizing the community about the importance of clean environments and hygiene. These community centers will be built with materials that are locally available and affordable. We shall therefore be focusing on materials such as earth blocks, bamboo sticks, metal, thatching grass, wood and rocks. The roofs of the centers will be water proof to ensure that the homes remain dry even during heavy rains. The homes will also be spacious and have several rooms so as to provide a number of activities and services to the community that are currently unavailable. We shall also be providing training and tools so that the community can develop some skills to construct their own homes and those of their neighbors. This will in the long run ensure that the community can provide for themselves and empower themselves as they become more independent. Environmental conservation. The communities we work in usually do not have any environmental facilities such as parks. As a result, they usually dump their garbage indiscriminately or burn it. This has been detrimental to their health because most of the children have asthma and other diseases. By creating parks, they will have a place to dispose of their garbage. The parks will also provide play grounds for the children in the community and will therefore reduce the cases of diseases such as asthma that are caused by indoor conditions. We shall also provide the necessary tools and skills so that the community can maintain and develop the parks on their own.

Old Cockie, who fathered a line of more manageable sheep dogs with the requisite willingness to work sheep. It was Old Cockie’s grandson, Wiston Cap, whose progeny founded the modern border collie breed in the 1900s. The modern border collie continues to be revered for its versatility, intelligence, and eagerness to please, and is the most popular working sheepdog in the world. Divider 1 Living Conditions Border collies are a herding dog at heart and enjoy being challenged. As such, they are happiest in a home where they have plenty of room to roam, with a fenced yard or access to a large field being preferable to an apartment. Border collies are more inclined to roam than many other breeds, and are known for their ability to jump tall fences, so they require a secure yard and close supervision. Border collies also have a long, coarse coat that makes them unsuitable for indoors, as their fur tends to shed profusely. They’re also prone to excessive barking, which can upset the neighbors. This makes them unsuitable for apartment-dwelling. Border collies are also prone to separation anxiety, and they need a lot of attention and stimulation to keep them happy. They’re not suitable for a family that will be away from the house for a long period. Border Collie Image Credit: Pixabay Border collies are very intelligent and trainable, provided that they’re given the opportunity to use their minds. As such, they’re best suited to an owner who has the time and patience to spend on their dog, with the willingness to train it extensively and provide it with daily challenges. When the border collie’s mind isn’t stimulated, it can quickly develop destructive behaviors, and they’re also prone to depressive behaviors if they don’t have enough attention from their owners. Border collies are also fairly easy to housebreak, and they’re very eager to please and respond well to training. As such, they’re not a good choice for an inexperienced dog owner, and should be left to someone who has the time and knowledge to properly train a border collie. The Consensus Curriculum is integrated into the specific process to strive toward a deeper understanding and proficiency of the concepts. The curriculum follows and advances the mission and vision of the Diocese of Richmond regarding faith-based education. The mission of the Consensus Curriculum is to provide students with a consistent curriculum, with rigorous standards, relative to their age and developmental stage. This will result in the students receiving a homogeneous curriculum that will support their advancement to the next intellectual level and beyond. Furthermore, the students will be prepared to compete successfully in college, the workforce, and in society, as a whole. The curriculum will also foster intellectual, critical thinking skills, while promoting personal, social, spiritual development. The Consensus Curriculum is designed to support critical thinking skills and cognitive development through the following methods: 1. Learning occurs through the development of critical thinking skills: applying information to a situation, analyzing information, categorizing information, comparing and contrasting information, drawing conclusions based on information, evaluating information, identifying information, inferring information, interpreting information, predicting information, reading information, recalling information, summarizing information, synthesizing information, and using information. 2. Learning occurs through the development of analysis skills: determine the elements of a concept, determine the purpose of a concept, recognize the process of a concept, recognize the results of a concept, apply analysis skills to a problem, apply analysis skills to evaluate information, and identify the analysis skills utilized to analyze a concept. 3. Learning occurs through the development of deductive and inductive reasoning skills: evaluate information, recognize similarities and differences in information, recognize the parts of information, recognize the qualities of information, and identify logic. 4. Learning occurs through the development of clarity of thought skills: organize information, use appropriate vocabulary, correct grammatical usage, and support a position with evidence. 5. Learning occurs through the development of problem solving skills: consider multiple strategies, evaluate the effectiveness of strategies, identify a problem, identify the goal, sequence the steps to solve the problem, utilize the problem-solving process, recognize when the problem is solved, and identify when a new problem develops. 6.
